top.title: West Ham interested in signing Arsenal youngster who is out on loan
top.description: West Ham interested in signing Arsenal youngster who is out on loan Ethan Nwaneri is facing an increasingly difficult situation at Borussia Dortmund, where he is spending the current season on loan . His future in Germany is now uncertain, with the possibility that his temporary spell could be brought to an end in January. Should that happen, the young midfielder already has a potential destination, with another club reportedly prepared to bring him into their squad for the remainder of the campaign. A move could provide him with an opportunity to regain his confidence and secure more regular playing time. Nwaneri is regarded as one of the finest young talents in the Arsenal squad and among the club’s most promising academy graduates in recent years. However, he is currently struggling to establish himself, both at the Emirates and during his loan spells away from North London . West Ham emerge as potential destination The youngster spent the second half of last season on loan at Olympique Marseille. His time in France initially showed considerable promise, but his situation deteriorated as the campaign progressed. A similar pattern appears to be developing during his current spell in Germany, raising questions about whether another change of environment would benefit his development. Despite these difficulties, Nwaneri will be hoping to turn his situation around and demonstrate his considerable potential. Arsenal, however, want him to play regularly and continue developing, which could prompt the club to consider recalling him when the January transfer window opens. West Ham have emerged as a possible destination should Arsenal decide to end his loan spell at Dortmund. According to Football365 , the Hammers regard Nwaneri as a valuable addition who could strengthen their squad for the remainder of the season. (Photo by Sona Maleterova/Getty Images) Loan move could offer fresh opportunity West Ham are keen to secure promotion back to the Premier League and believe that bringing in a player of Nwaneri’s quality could improve their chances. They are reportedly interested in signing him on loan for the second half of the campaign. Such a move could prove beneficial for the Arsenal youngster, particularly if it provides him with the regular opportunities he has struggled to secure in Germany. More consistent involvement would allow him to rebuild his confidence, gain valuable experience and demonstrate his abilities. For Arsenal, finding the right environment for Nwaneri’s development will remain important. top.title: Serena Williams’ former coach has noticed two big changes in Alexander Zverev as he becomes world number one
top.description: Alexander Zverev finally reached the summit of the ATP rankings after years of being a nearly man in men’s tennis. Zverev had cemented his status as the greatest player never to win a major up until Roland Garros earlier this season, where he secured his first Grand Slam title. After his triumph in Paris, the German reached his first Wimbledon final before clinching major number two at the US Open and ultimately becoming the world number one, rising above injured Jannik Sinner. Photo by Daniel Kopatsch/Getty Images Patrick Mouratoglou explains how Alexander Zverev has improved Zverev has faced criticism from pundits and fans alike since becoming the world number one, with some claiming he doesn’t deserve to sit atop the rankings due to his poor record against top-ten players and being winless against Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner in 2026. Others have come to the defence of Zverev, however, including Serena Williams’ former coach Patrick Mouratoglou. In a post on Instagram , Mouratoglou said: “Is Zverev better now than he was one year ago? Oh yes. “For two reasons. First, his serve has progressed a lot. It’s huge now; huge! The percentage of first serves is huge, the accuracy is huge, the speed is huge, the second serve is huge, everything is huge. “Secondly, yes, he is not the guy who has the ability to accelerate suddenly and make a big difference like Alcaraz, but if you look at the pace of the rallies, I think that Zverev is playing way faster than he was one year ago, and the big reason for that is because of his position. “He was two metres behind the baseline, and now he is just behind the baseline. He didn’t do this overnight, but he worked on it a lot to be able to position himself way closer to the baseline, and he still doesn’t make a lot of unforced errors, so he is super consistent while playing very close to the baseline at the same pace as before. So technically, because he is closer to the baseline, the rhythm of the rallies is way higher than before.” Zverev became the first German player in men’s tennis to reach the top of the rankings since Boris Becker in 1991. He also set the record for the fewest titles won by a year-end number one in a season with two.

top.title: 'He will win games single-handedly': Ex-cricketer backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World Cup
top.description: Former India captain and chief selector Kris Srikkanth has thrown his weight behind teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, backing him for opportunities across formats and urging the Indian team management to consider him for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Sooryavanshi has taken the cricketing world by storm with his extraordinary batting performances, showcasing remarkable power, timing and confidence at such a young age. Impressed by the youngster's fearless approach, Srikkanth believes Sooryavanshi has the potential to become an all-format cricketer and should not be restricted to a particular format. Speaking on his YouTube channel, the former India opener also suggested that the teenager should be considered for the upcoming ODI series against Sri Lanka. Kris Srikkanth backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World Cup Srikkanth believes Sooryavanshi deserves to be included in India's 15-member squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup, even if the team management is not yet convinced about his readiness for Test cricket. The former India selector stressed that the youngster should be given opportunities in the 50-over format to help him develop and gain experience at the international level. "He is an all-format player. You don't want to play him in Tests, okay, but at least keep him in the 15. There is no questioning now. Sri Lanka will be coming for ODIs, give him a chance there. Put him in and let him play ODIs against them. If you really want to develop Suryavanshi, take him to the 2027 World Cup. Let him be in the 15. One day he will win you games single-handedly," Srikkanth said on his Youtube Channel. Srikkanth compares Sooryavanshi with Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli Drawing comparisons with two of India's greatest batting icons, Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, Srikkanth went a step further by describing Sooryavanshi as the "son of the god of cricket". "The way he is batting, power alone is not enough. You need timing as well. It is not just about power, it is also about his confidence. He looked so still and calm. He does not look ruffled. The greatest thing is that he knows exactly what he is doing. This is genius. First came the god of cricket, Sachin Tendulkar, then the King Virat Kohli, and now he is the son of the god of cricket," he said. "If you do not encourage this guy and keep saying that he has to be groomed, it is unfair. You are going to spoil a cricketer this way. Team management and selectors, please wake up," he added.

top.title: No. 7 Miami Seniors Face Bittersweet Farewell Against Boston College
top.description: Credit USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Saturday marks a hard stop for the old guard at Hard Rock Stadium. The No. 7 Miami Hurricanes host Boston College for their final regular-season home game, and the atmosphere feels heavy with history. This is the last chance for players who spent their entire college careers in Coral Gables to say goodbye on home turf. It is a rare moment in a modern era where most players jump to the NFL after one or two years. The team stands at 10-1 with a perfect 8-0 record in the ACC, but the emotional stakes for the seniors are just as high as the playoff hunt. Senior defensive lineman Ahmad Moten Sr. knows the clock is running out. He spent five years building this defense and now faces the end of the line. “It’s definitely going to be a bittersweet moment. Last home game, last regular-season home game at Hard Rock … I’m not going to cry, of course, but it went by quick,” Moten said, according to Sun Sentinel . He admitted he didn’t believe his teammates when they warned him time would fly. Now he sees it all happened in a blink. The feeling is shared by running back Mark Fletcher Jr., who plans to savor every second before the final whistle. Standard of Play Must Stay High While the seniors get their flowers, head coach Mario Cristobal wants the team to keep playing with fire. The defense looked great against Virginia Tech, but the coach wasn’t happy with the slow start. Cristobal demands consistency from the first snap to the last. “We’ve got to play to our standard,” Cristobal said after the game, according to Sun Sentinel . He wants the speed and aggression seen in the final minutes to be there from the very beginning. That kind of intensity cannot be a switch that players flip only when the game is on the line. The coach believes the team needs to hunt down the quarterback with the same drive they showed late in the last contest. “That can’t be a switch because that is a different — if you watch it — it’s a different level of acceleration, hunting down the quarterback,” Cristobal said. The players agree that they need to fix their early-game lapses. Ahmad Moten Sr. told the team they must own their mistakes and get right. The defense gave up a long drive on the first possession against Virginia Tech but held the Hokies to just 133 yards after that. The goal is to make that strong finish the new normal. Recruiting Wins While Roster Turns Over Even as the current class finishes up, the program is already winning the next battle. To lock in the nation’s leading 2027 recruiting class, Miami secured five-star defensive end DJ Jacobs, flipping him from Ohio State. The move puts the Hurricanes ahead of every other school in the rankings. No other squad can equal Miami’s current total of seven five-star prospects within its class. top.title: Charles Leclerc explains Qatar GP practice spin after painfully "slow" day for Ferrari
top.description: Motorsport photo Charles Leclerc rued a "very, very difficult" FP2 for Ferrari at the Formula 1 Qatar Grand Prix, with his early spin the symptom of a general lack of grip in the SF-26. Having already gotten off to a quiet start in FP1, Leclerc and team-mate Lewis Hamilton could only manage seventh and eighth in FP2, a full second adrift of Mercedes' leader Kimi Antonelli . Read Also: F1 Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli leads Mercedes charge in twice red-flagged FP2 Not helping his cause, Leclerc suffered a violent spin exiting Turn 7 in the early stages of the session, sustaining floor damage that warranted a parts change mid-session. Leclerc explained that he had actually already damaged his floor earlier in the session over Lusail's notoriously high kerbs, and further damage following his excursion through the gravel trap forced Ferrari to change the floor entirely. "It's been just a very, very difficult session." Leclerc explained. "The best lap time was I think my first lap in FP2 and after that we could never really improve. Of course, we didn't do that many laps on the medium tyres because then we had to stop to repair because of the floor damage I got on the kerbs. "After I lost the car it probably made it even worse, so we just decided to change the floor which cost us quite a bit of time." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Ferrari sporting director Diego Ioverno explained: "After the spin there was clear damage on the floor. We saw it also from numbers, and we told him to stop. It was not repairable, so we replaced the floor. After that, there were still some small damages around the car, but nothing major." Leclerc didn't call in his floor damage as an excuse for the team's lack of pace, though, as also evidenced by Hamilton's poor pace as he reported a lack of rear grip. "To be honest, this is not even the reason why we were slow. We were just very slow from the first lap this morning to the last lap in FP2 and it's very difficult to understand what the outlier is," Leclerc acknowledged. With its many high downforce corners, motorcycle circuit Lusail is a track that the Ferrari SF-26 could have been expected to be competitive on, so the team is now poring over the data to find solutions overnight. "I really think there's an outlier that we need to find," Leclerc added. "At the moment, we just didn't quite put our finger on it, but we'll keep working in order to turn the situation around tomorrow. Overall, the pace has just been very, very poor. Low fuel, high fuel, normally high fuel is our strength, but today, there was just no pace at all. I don't really have an idea of what we can do significantly better that will turn the situation upside down." top.title: Man United make decision over Bruno Fernandes’ future
top.description: Man United make decision over Bruno Fernandes’ future Bruno Fernandes transfer latest as Manchester United move to protect valuation Manchester United are preparing for a significant decision on Bruno Fernandes, with the club understood to be moving to secure their position by triggering the one-year extension in his current deal. According to TeamTalk , that step would keep the Portugal international tied to Old Trafford until 2028 and, crucially, strengthen United’s hand if his future becomes a live transfer issue. top.title: Blues Need Grit To Beat Stars In Tight Central Race
top.description: Joe Puetz-Imagn Images The Central Division is a mess, and the St. Louis Blues are stuck right in the middle of it. Dallas holds second place, but the gap to sixth place is just three points. That tiny margin means every single point matters. The Blues lost their four-game winning streak on Wednesday night in a shootout against the New York Islanders. Now they face a Dallas team that just saw its own five-game run end with a loss to Nashville. Both clubs are tired, but only one will survive Friday’s matchup in St. Louis. A Road Record That Matters Dallas has been nearly unbeatable on the road this season. Away from home, the Stars have posted a 6-1-2 record, having lost just once in regulation time. That is the fewest road losses in the entire league, per Field Level Media . It is a stat that hurts St. Louis right now. The Blues need to stop the bleeding if they want to climb the standings. A loss here would be a massive blow to their playoff hopes in such a crowded division. They cannot afford to let the Stars build a bigger cushion. Keys Missing for St. Louis The Blues are dealing with a nasty injury bug that could cost them the game. Forward Jimmy Snuggerud leads the team with 14 goals and 20 points, but he is out with an upper-body injury. Pavel Buchnevich is also listed as day-to-day due to a similar issue. These two players drive the offense, and their absence changes everything. Dallas coach Glen Gulutzan admitted his team was flat after losing to Nashville, noting, “This one is going to leave a sour taste in everyone’s mouth — players, coaches, everybody.” If the Blues can’t find a way to score without their top scorers, they will struggle against a Dallas defense that has been solid. Can They Bounce Back? St. Louis showed some heart on Wednesday when they forced overtime against the Islanders. Mason McTavish scored for the Blues, and the team showed they could compete even in a loss. “I loved our effort, I loved our grit,” St. Louis coach Jim Montgomery said after the game. He added, “I thought we played an intelligent road game.” The Blues need that same energy on Friday. They have a chance to prove they belong in the top half of the Central.

top.title: Ogun 2027: Court dismisses Hunye’s suits against Adeola’s APC candidacy
top.description: …Adeola hails judgment …as Hunye heads to Court of Appeal By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Federal High Court sitting in Abeokuta, Ogun State, on Friday dismissed two suits filed by Hon. Abayomi Semako Hunye challenging the emergence of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Delivering judgment in the two consolidated suits, Justice Okeke held that the cases lacked merit and consequently dismissed them. The suits, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1127/2026 and FHC/AB/126/2026, were instituted by Hunye against the APC, Senator Adeola and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), challenging the process through which Adeola emerged as the party’s governorship candidate. Reacting to the judgment, Adeola commended the judiciary, describing the decision as a vindication of the rule of law and the judicial process. In a statement issued by his media adviser, Chief Kayode Odunaro, the senator expressed satisfaction with the outcome while appreciating his legal team for what he described as their painstaking efforts in defending the suits. Adeola said, “I want to commend the Honourable Justice for his erudite judgment in these cases challenging my overwhelming and widely accepted victory in our party primary. I also commend my legal team for the painstaking defense put up during the process. “This victory is yet another milestone in our quest for equity and justice in the Ogun State 2027 election. To God be the glory once again.” The senator said that despite the legal challenges, he had remained focused on consolidating support for his candidacy across the state through engagements with political stakeholders and other interest groups. He added that his engagements had also included the presentation of his nine-pillar ITESIWAJU Agenda, which he described as his development blueprint for Ogun State. According to him, the court’s decision would allow him to concentrate more fully on preparations for the 2027 governorship election and take his campaign message to voters across the state. Adeola also urged APC members and his supporters, irrespective of their political affiliations, to remain united and focused, stressing that his ambition was driven by a desire to serve the people and contribute to the development of Ogun State. However, Hunye has rejected the outcome of the proceedings and indicated his intention to appeal the judgment. In a statement titled, “Our Legal Journey Continues to the Court of Appeal,” Hunye described the Federal High Court as the first stage of the judicial process, insisting that the appellate court would provide another opportunity for his legal team to pursue the issues raised in the suits. He reaffirmed his commitment to constitutional due process, internal party democracy, and the rule of law, saying his decision to continue with the litigation was informed by the need to ensure fairness and strict compliance with establi

nigeria.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
nigeria.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. The reported immigration charges do not amount to convictions for romance fraud. The post Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Adesua Etomi celebrates negative cancer test
nigeria.description: Nollywood actress Adesua Etomi-Wellington has celebrated testing negative for cancer after months of medical procedures, hospital visits and uncertainty over her health. The actress announced the development on Friday in an Instagram video, expressing gratitude to God following the latest result from her medical tests. “The doctor just called me back with the result from the lab, no cancer… God is good,” she said. The video showed some of the medical procedures she underwent, while other pictures revealed bruises on her body and redness beneath one of her eyes. Etomi-Wellington also shared a video of friends and well-wishers celebrating the result with her. Reflecting on her experience, the actress described 2026 as one of the most difficult periods of her life, explaining that her reduced public appearances were linked to her health struggles. “2026 really tried it. I know I’ve been quieter than usual this year (and that’s saying something), but behind the silence were some of the most difficult months of my life,” she wrote. She disclosed that the ordeal involved several medical procedures, scans, injections and hospital visits, adding that she received treatment from medical teams in Nigeria and the United States. “This year threw everything at me, but by the grace of God, I am NOT EASILY BROKEN,” she added. The actress also expressed appreciation to her husband, singer and politician Bankole Wellington, popularly known as Banky W, their children, friends and family members for supporting her throughout the difficult period. “To my friends and family who prayed for me, stood in the gap and held me through some of my darkest days, I will never take your love for granted,” she wrote. The health update comes two days after the couple released a gospel song, On My Way , on November 25 to celebrate their ninth wedding anniversary. The track, credited to Etomi-Wellington, who performs under the musical name Susu, and Banky W, is the lead single from their forthcoming joint album, Not Easily Broken , expected in 2027. The actress described the song as “the soundtrack to our testimony and thanksgiving”, linking its message to their personal experiences. The couple have previously spoken about their health challenges. In May 2024, Banky W disclosed that he had undergone his fourth surgery for cancer after earlier procedures to remove cancerous tumours. Etomi-Wellington also revealed in March 2025 that she battled hyperemesis gravidarum, a severe form of pregnancy sickness, during her second pregnancy. The condition left her ill for months and required hospitalisation before she underwent an emergency Caesarean section. nigeria.title: UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax
nigeria.description: The United Kingdom government has outlined two conditions under which travellers can bring goods into the country without paying customs duty or tax, warning that items outside the permitted categories or allowance limits could attract charges. According to the UK government’s customs guidelines, travellers can bring goods into the country tax-free under two conditions. First condition is personal use. Goods must be intended for the traveller’s own use rather than for commercial purposes or resale. Second condition is gifts. Travellers can also bring goods intended as presents for other people without paying customs duty, provided they remain within the applicable personal allowance. The rules apply to foreign visitors and British residents returning from overseas, regardless of whether the items were purchased from regular shops or duty-free outlets at airports. However, the exemptions are subject to personal allowance limits, which determine the quantity and value of goods travellers can bring into the country without incurring additional charges. The applicable allowance depends on where a traveller is arriving from and whether the destination is Great Britain, comprising England, Scotland and Wales, or Northern Ireland. The government also warned that goods intended for business or resale do not qualify for personal allowances. Such items must be declared to customs regardless of their value or quantity. Travellers are also required to declare goods that exceed their personal allowances or fall under banned and restricted categories before crossing the border. Declarations can be made online up to five days, or 120 hours, before arrival in the UK. The authorities warned that failure to comply with customs regulations could result in the seizure of goods and, in some cases, the vehicle used to transport them. nigeria.title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda
nigeria.description: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine launched in Uganda on Friday, while a global NGO said it had bought 1.5 million doses of another candidate, as the race heats up to contain the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the outbreak in DRC, which has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases since being declared in May, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Two experimental vaccines are due to start testing on Monday in the outbreak’s epicentre in eastern DRC, the WHO said, focusing on contacts of cases and people deemed at high risk of infection. But neighbouring Uganda announced it had also launched a trial of one of the vaccines, developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid pandemic. The Uganda Virus Research Institute described it as “Africa’s first mRNA Phase I clinical trial”, conducted in collaboration with Moderna. It will test 224 healthy volunteers aged between one and 65 to measure its safety and immunity potential. The other potential vaccine is the ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector vaccine developed by India’s Serum Institute and the University of Oxford — which will also begin testing in DRC on Monday. But Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which brings together government and private donors to help developing countries acquire jabs at affordable prices, is not waiting around. After the Covid-19 pandemic, the alliance set up a new $50 million First Response Fund — under a so-called “No Regrets” approach — to allow it to buy up doses in advance even before they have been fully tested. – Deployment – Gavi signed a purchase commitment this week with the Serum Institute for 1.5 million doses of the ChAdOx1, and plans to have “hundreds of thousands” ready to deploy should the trials prove successful and they are approved by the WHO and DRC government. “We’re investing in it, hoping that the signals will be positive, and if that is the case, we’ll have gained months and months on the deployment,” Emanuele Capobianco, Gavi’s director of global health security, told AFP. He said he hoped for trials to conclude “within the first half of 2027” and even “within the first quarter” in a more optimistic scenario. Gavi also has a stockpile of 500,000 doses of an existing vaccine, Ervebo, used against the Zaire strain of Ebola, which began testing last month to see if it is also effective against Bundibugyo. Despite a long and porous border with eastern DRC, Uganda has successfully contained the virus after receiving some imported cases earlier this year. It was declared Ebola-free in August after registering 20 cases, including two deaths. The post mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Nigeria set to bid to host maiden U-17 WAFCON
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigeria is preparing to bid to host the maiden edition of the Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), as the country seeks to attract more international sporting competitions and strengthen its sports economy. The Director-General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Bukola Olopade, disclosed this in a video shared on his X handle on Friday, saying Nigeria had already communicated its interest to the Confederation of African Football (CAF). According to Olopade, the country expressed its desire to host the competition during CAF’s General Assembly held in Abuja last weekend. “We have said to CAF that we are desirous of hosting the first Under-17 women’s championship,” he said. He explained that the move forms part of Nigeria’s ambition to move away from what he described as a consuming sports economy towards a productive one, where hosting international events would generate economic benefits for the country. “We don’t want to be a consuming sports economy; rather, we want to be a productive sports economy. We want to attract more international events where the economic impacts will be felt by the people,” Olopade added. CAF’s Executive Committee approved the introduction of the U-17 WAFCON on November 21, with the inaugural tournament scheduled to take place between March and April 2028. Qualifying matches are expected to begin in April 2027. Nigeria’s interest in hosting the competition comes amid discussions about the country’s readiness to stage major international football events. Earlier this week, FIFA President Gianni Infantino said Nigeria was not yet ready to host the men’s FIFA World Cup, although he acknowledged the country’s resources, passion and willingness to stage the competition. Infantino, however, suggested that Nigeria could demonstrate its organisational capacity by hosting smaller international football tournaments before taking on events of greater magnitude. The proposed U-17 WAFCON could therefore provide Nigeria with an opportunity to showcase its capacity to organise a continental football competition. nigeria.title: Hackers breach US Air Force Cloud computing platform
nigeria.description: Hackers have breached Cloud One, the United States Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, potentially exposing sensitive military, personnel and logistics data. Three people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the intrusion was discovered within the past month during efforts to upgrade the system, triggering disruptions across the platform. However, the identity of the hackers, the full extent of the breach and whether any data was stolen remain unknown. In a statement to Reuters, the US Air Force declined to discuss the security status of specific networks and systems. It said: “We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities.” A major military computing platform Launched in 2017, Cloud One was designed as a centralised platform for the Air Force’s information technology needs, bringing together services provided by four major technology companies: Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet. The platform supports dozens of applications, including systems managing personnel records, salaries, logistics and military equipment maintenance. Among the applications hosted on Cloud One are the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control system, which consolidates air defence radar and other data feeds across North America, and the Theatre Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles at more than 200 US Air Force locations worldwide. Cloud One is regarded as one of the US military’s largest cloud computing platforms, according to two sources familiar with the matter. “A breach here is a big deal,” one of the sources told Reuters. Investigators have reportedly involved US Cyber Command, the military’s cyber warfare arm, to assess the damage. Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) served as the platform’s prime contractor until 2025, when Leidos took over the contract. SAIC did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment, while Leidos referred questions to the Air Force. Breach disrupts military operations The intrusion has reportedly triggered several disruptions across the platform. Two sources and another person familiar with the matter said plans to migrate additional back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, had been suspended. Updates to applications already running on the platform were also blocked, preventing Air Force personnel from installing fixes, even as new software vulnerabilities were being disclosed across the technology industry. Another source said some users had their administrator privileges revoked. One of the sources said the hackers exploited a software vulnerability to gain access to the platform’s control plane, which manages and oversees the underlying cloud infrastructure. The source likened the control plane to a universal remote, explaining that access could theoretically allow intruders to check the operational status of military aircraft or monitor the movement of spare

nigeria.title: France slips into ‘technical recession’ after GDP revision
nigeria.description: France’s economy has slipped into a technical recession after revised official figures showed that gross domestic product (GDP) contracted in the third quarter, extending the country’s economic decline. The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) said on Friday that the eurozone’s second-largest economy shrank by 0.2 per cent in the third quarter, revising its initial estimate of a 0.1 per cent contraction. The agency also revised second-quarter growth downwards to 0.02 per cent from zero per cent previously, although the figure was rounded to zero in the headline data. The revisions mean France’s economy has recorded consecutive quarterly contractions since the end of last year, meeting the conventional definition of a technical recession, which is two successive quarters of negative economic growth. The latest figures pose additional challenges for the government as it struggles to rein in the country’s budget deficit, with its target of 0.5 per cent economic growth this year now appearing increasingly difficult to achieve. The minority government is also facing difficulties securing parliamentary approval for its 2027 budget, which seeks to reduce the fiscal deficit from 5.4 per cent of GDP this year to five per cent next year. The budget debate comes five months before France’s presidential election, amid deep divisions in parliament. Reacting to the figures, Finance Minister Roland Lescure called for the speedy adoption of the budget, insisting that the five per cent deficit target was non-negotiable. “We must adopt a budget as soon as possible with a non-negotiable deficit target of 5%. It is imperative that we restore visibility for economic stakeholders,” he said. A breakdown of the third-quarter GDP figures by INSEE showed that weak domestic demand contributed to the contraction. Consumer spending rose by 0.3 per cent, but this was offset by a 0.8 per cent decline in business investment. The rebuilding of business inventories contributed 0.3 percentage points to GDP growth, following a 0.7 percentage-point reduction in the previous quarter. Foreign trade also weighed heavily on economic performance, subtracting 0.6 percentage points from output as exports fell by 1.6 per cent while imports increased by 0.1 per cent. Despite the contraction, the Bank of France said earlier in November that the economy was expected to record moderate growth in the fourth quarter. nigeria.title: Kebbi Police probe alleged importation of political thugs
nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The Kebbi State Police Command has launched an investigation into a viral video showing suspected political thugs brandishing dangerous weapons and issuing threats capable of undermining public peace and security in the state. The command also said it had invited three persons mentioned in the video for questioning over the circumstances surrounding the presence of the suspected thugs in Kebbi State. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Bashir Usman, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, saying intelligence reports and preliminary scrutiny of the video identified one “Mai Barewa”, described as a notorious thug from Sokoto State, alongside other individuals wielding dangerous weapons and making threatening statements. According to Usman, the individuals were heard in the video claiming to have responded to an invitation and mentioning three persons identified as Manu Gwanna, Bashar S. A. and Khairullah Jega in connection with their presence in the state. He described the threats, particularly those directed at individuals perceived not to support the ruling party, as a potential recipe for political violence. The police spokesman said the persons mentioned and identified in the video had been invited to assist the ongoing investigation, while the command was taking steps to identify, apprehend and prosecute Mai Barewa and his accomplices. He said the police would ensure that anyone found culpable was dealt with in accordance with the law. The command reiterated its commitment to political neutrality, impartial law enforcement and the protection of all citizens, irrespective of their political affiliations. It warned that no political party, individual or group would be allowed to undermine peaceful electioneering, intimidate citizens or engage in violence under the guise of political activities. The statement noted that Kebbi had long enjoyed a peaceful political climate, which must be preserved ahead of the 2027 general elections. Consequently, the police warned political parties, their leaders, supporters and associates against recruiting, harbouring, mobilising or sponsoring suspected imported thugs, or engaging in any conduct capable of inciting violence and disrupting political stability. The command further warned that it would not allow political violence, intimidation and lawlessness to take root in the state or set a dangerous precedent ahead of the 2027 elections. It urged residents to remain calm, refrain from taking the law into their own hands and promptly report suspicious activities to the nearest police station or through the command’s designated communication channels. The police assured residents of its commitment to maintaining peace, protecting lives and property, and ensuring that all political activities in the state are conducted within the ambit of the law. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Fully Lifts Withdrawal Suspension a Month After $6.3 Billion Hack Binance has fully lifted the withdrawal suspension it put in place after last month’s record $6.3 billion hack, saying its recovery work is complete and that withdrawals are open across nearly all networks. “Our withdrawal recovery work is completed and the withdrawal suspension from the security incident has been fully lifted,” the exchange said in an X post Thursday afternoon. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. North Korean launderers have stepped up transfers through THORChain and a coinjoin service in recent days, blockchain researchers told Reuters , as part of an operation spanning tens of thousands of transactions across blockchains. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008. Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m. Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%. Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Galaxy Withdraws Call That Bitcoin’s Bear Market Ended in June Galaxy has withdrawn its October call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June, saying the technical signal behind it failed after seven straight weeks of losses and that the bear market is “very likely not over.” Alex Thorn, Galaxy’s head of firmwide research, laid out the reversal in a report published Wednesday and sent to clients a day earlier. “We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June,” the report said. “The signal it rested on has failed.” The firm’s Oct. 26 note had argued that bitcoin had entered an accumulation phase. Galaxy said at the time that a weekly close back below the 50-week moving average that was not regained within a month would invalidate its technical case. That is what happened. Bitcoin closed the week ended Nov. 8 at $74,968, 0.7% below the 50-week average, after seven weekly closes above it. It then closed the week ended Nov. 15 below the 200-week average, which Galaxy has described as the floor of past bear markets. Galaxy points to $58,525 The week ended Nov. 22 closed at $61,104, 17.9% below the 50-week average and 10.4% below the 200-week average of $68,159. Bitcoin traded below its July 1 intraday low on Nov. 20 and reached $55,100 on Nov. 21, but the June 30 closing low of $58,525 held on a daily basis through Nov. 22. Galaxy now treats that level as the line to watch. A daily close below $58,525 would be “the start of a move to a materially lower low,” the report said, and the firm would not treat such a close as a buying signal by itself. History is not kind to breaks like that. In the seven prior bear market cases where bitcoin closed below a low that had stood for at least 60 days, the eventual low was at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%. Applied to the June low, that works out to about $48,500 and $28,200. Bitcoin briefly slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday morning as the Nasdaq sank, but it ended the day back above $60,000 and has not posted a daily close below $58,525. It traded near $60,800 on Thursday morning. Late by the clock, early by the depth Galaxy said two readings of the market disagree. By the calendar, this bear is old: Nov. 22 was day 412 since the Oct. 6, 2025, record, longer than the 163 to 406 days from high to low in the four prior bear markets. By depth, it looks unfinished. Bitcoin’s 53% decline compares with drops of 77% to 93% in earlier bears. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. sports.title: Serena Williams’ former coach has noticed two big changes in Alexander Zverev as he becomes world number one
sports.description: Alexander Zverev finally reached the summit of the ATP rankings after years of being a nearly man in men’s tennis. Zverev had cemented his status as the greatest player never to win a major up until Roland Garros earlier this season, where he secured his first Grand Slam title. After his triumph in Paris, the German reached his first Wimbledon final before clinching major number two at the US Open and ultimately becoming the world number one, rising above injured Jannik Sinner. Photo by Daniel Kopatsch/Getty Images Patrick Mouratoglou explains how Alexander Zverev has improved Zverev has faced criticism from pundits and fans alike since becoming the world number one, with some claiming he doesn’t deserve to sit atop the rankings due to his poor record against top-ten players and being winless against Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner in 2026. Others have come to the defence of Zverev, however, including Serena Williams’ former coach Patrick Mouratoglou. In a post on Instagram , Mouratoglou said: “Is Zverev better now than he was one year ago? Oh yes. “For two reasons. First, his serve has progressed a lot. It’s huge now; huge! The percentage of first serves is huge, the accuracy is huge, the speed is huge, the second serve is huge, everything is huge. “Secondly, yes, he is not the guy who has the ability to accelerate suddenly and make a big difference like Alcaraz, but if you look at the pace of the rallies, I think that Zverev is playing way faster than he was one year ago, and the big reason for that is because of his position. “He was two metres behind the baseline, and now he is just behind the baseline. He didn’t do this overnight, but he worked on it a lot to be able to position himself way closer to the baseline, and he still doesn’t make a lot of unforced errors, so he is super consistent while playing very close to the baseline at the same pace as before. So technically, because he is closer to the baseline, the rhythm of the rallies is way higher than before.” Zverev became the first German player in men’s tennis to reach the top of the rankings since Boris Becker in 1991. He also set the record for the fewest titles won by a year-end number one in a season with two.

sports.title: 'He will win games single-handedly': Ex-cricketer backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World Cup
sports.description: Former India captain and chief selector Kris Srikkanth has thrown his weight behind teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, backing him for opportunities across formats and urging the Indian team management to consider him for the 2027 ODI World Cup. Sooryavanshi has taken the cricketing world by storm with his extraordinary batting performances, showcasing remarkable power, timing and confidence at such a young age. Impressed by the youngster's fearless approach, Srikkanth believes Sooryavanshi has the potential to become an all-format cricketer and should not be restricted to a particular format. Speaking on his YouTube channel, the former India opener also suggested that the teenager should be considered for the upcoming ODI series against Sri Lanka. Kris Srikkanth backs Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 2027 ODI World Cup Srikkanth believes Sooryavanshi deserves to be included in India's 15-member squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup, even if the team management is not yet convinced about his readiness for Test cricket. The former India selector stressed that the youngster should be given opportunities in the 50-over format to help him develop and gain experience at the international level. "He is an all-format player. You don't want to play him in Tests, okay, but at least keep him in the 15. There is no questioning now. Sri Lanka will be coming for ODIs, give him a chance there. Put him in and let him play ODIs against them. If you really want to develop Suryavanshi, take him to the 2027 World Cup. Let him be in the 15. One day he will win you games single-handedly," Srikkanth said on his Youtube Channel. Srikkanth compares Sooryavanshi with Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli Drawing comparisons with two of India's greatest batting icons, Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli, Srikkanth went a step further by describing Sooryavanshi as the "son of the god of cricket". "The way he is batting, power alone is not enough. You need timing as well. It is not just about power, it is also about his confidence. He looked so still and calm. He does not look ruffled. The greatest thing is that he knows exactly what he is doing. This is genius. First came the god of cricket, Sachin Tendulkar, then the King Virat Kohli, and now he is the son of the god of cricket," he said. "If you do not encourage this guy and keep saying that he has to be groomed, it is unfair. You are going to spoil a cricketer this way. Team management and selectors, please wake up," he added.

sports.title: No. 7 Miami Seniors Face Bittersweet Farewell Against Boston College
sports.description: Credit USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Saturday marks a hard stop for the old guard at Hard Rock Stadium. The No. 7 Miami Hurricanes host Boston College for their final regular-season home game, and the atmosphere feels heavy with history. This is the last chance for players who spent their entire college careers in Coral Gables to say goodbye on home turf. It is a rare moment in a modern era where most players jump to the NFL after one or two years. The team stands at 10-1 with a perfect 8-0 record in the ACC, but the emotional stakes for the seniors are just as high as the playoff hunt. Senior defensive lineman Ahmad Moten Sr. knows the clock is running out. He spent five years building this defense and now faces the end of the line. “It’s definitely going to be a bittersweet moment. Last home game, last regular-season home game at Hard Rock … I’m not going to cry, of course, but it went by quick,” Moten said, according to Sun Sentinel . He admitted he didn’t believe his teammates when they warned him time would fly. Now he sees it all happened in a blink. The feeling is shared by running back Mark Fletcher Jr., who plans to savor every second before the final whistle. Standard of Play Must Stay High While the seniors get their flowers, head coach Mario Cristobal wants the team to keep playing with fire. The defense looked great against Virginia Tech, but the coach wasn’t happy with the slow start. Cristobal demands consistency from the first snap to the last. “We’ve got to play to our standard,” Cristobal said after the game, according to Sun Sentinel . He wants the speed and aggression seen in the final minutes to be there from the very beginning. That kind of intensity cannot be a switch that players flip only when the game is on the line. The coach believes the team needs to hunt down the quarterback with the same drive they showed late in the last contest. “That can’t be a switch because that is a different — if you watch it — it’s a different level of acceleration, hunting down the quarterback,” Cristobal said. The players agree that they need to fix their early-game lapses. Ahmad Moten Sr. told the team they must own their mistakes and get right. The defense gave up a long drive on the first possession against Virginia Tech but held the Hokies to just 133 yards after that. The goal is to make that strong finish the new normal. To lock in the nation’s leading 2027 recruiting class, Miami secured five-star defensive end DJ Jacobs, flipping him from Ohio State. Leclerc explained that he had actually already damaged his floor earlier in the session over Lusail's notoriously high kerbs, and further damage following his excursion through the gravel trap forced Ferrari to change the floor entirely. "It's been just a very, very difficult session." Leclerc explained. "The best lap time was I think my first lap in FP2 and after that we could never really improve. Of course, we didn't do that many laps on the medium tyres because then we had to stop to repair because of the floor damage I got on the kerbs. "After I lost the car it probably made it even worse, so we just decided to change the floor which cost us quite a bit of time." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Ferrari sporting director Diego Ioverno explained: "After the spin there was clear damage on the floor. We saw it also from numbers, and we told him to stop. It was not repairable, so we replaced the floor. After that, there were still some small damages around the car, but nothing major." Leclerc didn't call in his floor damage as an excuse for the team's lack of pace, though, as also evidenced by Hamilton's poor pace as he reported a lack of rear grip. "To be honest, this is not even the reason why we were slow. We were just very slow from the first lap this morning to the last lap in FP2 and it's very difficult to understand what the outlier is," Leclerc acknowledged. With its many high downforce corners, motorcycle circuit Lusail is a track that the Ferrari SF-26 could have been expected to be competitive on, so the team is now poring over the data to find solutions overnight. "I really think there's an outlier that we need to find," Leclerc added. "At the moment, we just didn't quite put our finger on it, but we'll keep working in order to turn the situation around tomorrow. Overall, the pace has just been very, very poor. Low fuel, high fuel, normally high fuel is our strength, but today, there was just no pace at all. I don't really have an idea of what we can do significantly better that will turn the situation upside down." Ferrari also lost Hamilton to a power unit failure in the closing stages of an extended practice session, but as the seven-time world champion was running an older power unit for practice before turning to a fresher one overnight, his failure was not much of a concern, said Leclerc

sports.title: Blues Need Grit To Beat Stars In Tight Central Race
sports.description: Joe Puetz-Imagn Images The Central Division is a mess, and the St. Louis Blues are stuck right in the middle of it. Dallas holds second place, but the gap to sixth place is just three points. That tiny margin means every single point matters. The Blues lost their four-game winning streak on Wednesday night in a shootout against the New York Islanders. Now they face a Dallas team that just saw its own five-game run end with a loss to Nashville. Both clubs are tired, but only one will survive Friday’s matchup in St. Louis. A Road Record That Matters Dallas has been nearly unbeatable on the road this season. Away from home, the Stars have posted a 6-1-2 record, having lost just once in regulation time. That is the fewest road losses in the entire league, per Field Level Media . It is a stat that hurts St. Louis right now. The Blues need to stop the bleeding if they want to climb the standings. A loss here would be a massive blow to their playoff hopes in such a crowded division. They cannot afford to let the Stars build a bigger cushion. Keys Missing for St. Louis The Blues are dealing with a nasty injury bug that could cost them the game. Forward Jimmy Snuggerud leads the team with 14 goals and 20 points, but he is out with an upper-body injury. Pavel Buchnevich is also listed as day-to-day due to a similar issue. These two players drive the offense, and their absence changes everything. Dallas coach Glen Gulutzan admitted his team was flat after losing to Nashville, noting, “This one is going to leave a sour taste in everyone’s mouth — players, coaches, everybody.” If the Blues can’t find a way to score without their top scorers, they will struggle against a Dallas defense that has been solid. Can They Bounce Back? St. Louis showed some heart on Wednesday when they forced overtime against the Islanders. Mason McTavish scored for the Blues, and the team showed they could compete even in a loss. “I loved our effort, I loved our grit,” St. Louis coach Jim Montgomery said after the game. He added, “I thought we played an intelligent road game.” The Blues need that same energy on Friday. They have a chance to prove they belong in the top half of the Central.

technology.title: Smartphone shipments face another bleak year before modest 2028 comeback
technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. That's the outlook from Counterpoint Research's latest Smartphone Market Outlook Tracker , which points to rising memory costs and constrained supplies as continuing pressure on handset makers and buyers. The downturn was particularly sharp in the third quarter: IDC and Omdia estimated year-on-year shipment declines of 22 percent and 20 percent respectively, as rising prices and component shortages squeezed the market. Don't expect things to get better in the short term, as Counterpoint forecasts another 6 percent drop during 2027. But it believes that the market may see a 6 percent rebound in 2028, as memory supplies improve, pricing begins to stabilize, and pent-up demand for replacement phones returns. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. According to IDC , memory costs have risen approximately 350 percent since last year and are still climbing. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. "Mobile memory allocation is still being displaced by AI and server demand, while higher costs are taking longer to move through handset portfolios and retail channels. The result is a much weaker 2027, particularly for lower priced devices and price sensitive markets." Global shipments are forecast to rebound by 6 percent in 2028, but that would bring shipments only roughly back to this year's already shrunken level, rather than hitting the peak of previous years. Counterpoint cautions that the scale of the rebound will depend on how quickly lower component costs translate into retail pricing. A speedy improvement in mobile memory allocation during the second half of 2027 could bring replacement demand forward and swell shipments, but continued competition from the AI market or another round of handset price increases would hinder recovery. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026.
